script: NBA players who never got to wear the jersey number they actually wanted! When Kobe Bryant was a freshman at Lower Merion High School, he wore number twenty-four, then switched to thirty-three as a tribute to his dad, Joe “Jellybean” Bryant, who wore that same number back in high school. So when the seventeen-year-old got traded to the Los Angeles Lakers on draft night in nineteen ninety-six, he wanted to bring his dad's number with him. But there was a problem he didn't see coming. Thirty-three was already hanging in the rafters because the Lakers had retired it six years earlier for Kareem Abdul-Jabbar. So okay, Kobe figures he'll just go back to twenty-four, the number he started with in high school, except a veteran named Fred Roberts was already wearing it on the roster. The Lakers released Roberts just five days after Kobe's first press conference, which means he barely missed his chance at getting twenty-four. Both jerseys that meant something to him were completely off the table, and a seventeen-year-old rookie had nothing to put on his back. But that's when Kobe did something only Kobe would do. He thought back to the Adidas ABCD Camp where he played as a high school star and remembered his jersey number was one forty-three. He added up the digits, one plus four plus three equals eight, which also happened to be the number he wore growing up in Italy. And that piece of math became one of the most iconic numbers in basketball history. Kobe wore number eight for ten straight seasons before he finally switched back to twenty-four, the number he wanted all along, and the Lakers eventually retired both of them.
